title: High-Pass Filter - WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for Public Safety Band Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a High-Pass Filter filter targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz) for Public Safety Band Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on Si substrate with a target center frequency of 5432.8 MHz and bandwidth of 327.9 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the Public Safety Band Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: High-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: WiFi 6E (6 GHz)
- Application: Public Safety Band Filter
- Substrate: AlN on Si
- Package: CSP (Chip Scale Package)
- Design Tool: Ansys HFSS 2024R1
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the High-Pass Filter design targeting WiFi 6E (6 GHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       5432.8 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       327.9 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 11.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 35.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 17.0 dB
Q Factor:               7491
Temperature Coefficient:-14.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.9 x 1.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   12
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Ansys HFSS 2024R1 and load the High-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on Si with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 5432.8 MHz, BW 327.9 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (CSP (Chip Scale Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on Si).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight E5080B ENA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 16298 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 11.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 492 MHz offset >= 35.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 8 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 9.6 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +31 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 88%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2025-03-02
Devices Tested:         65
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.07 dB
Return Loss (meas):     12.8 dB
Rejection (meas):       38.2 dB
Isolation (meas):       22.0 dB
Q Factor (meas):        7491
Group Delay Variation:  3.1 ns
Power Handling:         +33 dBm
Die Yield:              80.2%

Result Classification:  FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The High-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for WiFi 6E (6 GHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Simulation-to-measurement correlation was within 3% for all key parameters.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Optimize resonator geometry to reduce insertion loss by ~0.3 dB.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Escalate to advanced materials team for alternative piezoelectric stack.
